why: The `routing` a kind:44221 session.create carries is the RECORD — the host's whole answer, written after it intersected its registry with its own live catalog. One record per request in hire-request-fixture.json, in the same order, so the pair reads as question and answer. buzz-core's `Routing` is canonical; this file pins the desktop, web and mobile observers to the same bytes.

keys.note: Every key under `always` is written, `null` where unanswered, so a strict observer has exactly one shape to accept — including `profile: null`, which is what the CLI and buzz-core emit when the lead asked for no extra minimums. `proposedDisagreement` is present only when the host's own choice differs from the `proposed` decision the request carried, and it is one sentence naming the difference. A record that silently replaced a requester's proposal would be the host routing behind the requester's back.

records.case: fast builder, no override — the host agrees with what was proposed

routing.reason: cleared the builder gates and the fast tier's low effort; cheapest expected accepted completion of the eligible targets.

records.case: standard builder — the override is honoured and recorded, and the router's own pick survives as the runner-up

routing.reason: human override: Brian asked for the big one on this lane. The router would have chosen claude-primary/sonnet (medium), which is recorded as the runner-up.

override.because: Brian asked for the big one on this lane.

records.case: deep architect — the host disagrees with the proposal and says so

routing.reason: cleared the architect gates and the deep tier's high effort; cheapest expected accepted completion of the eligible targets on this host's live catalog.
routing.proposedDisagreement: the request proposed codex-primary/gpt-5.6-sol (high); this host routed claude-primary/opus[1m] (high) because the seat's identity runs on claude-primary and codex-primary is not in this seat's catalog.
